metaDescription: Eighty Four sits in Washington County's active Marcellus wet-gas core. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, cash offer, no broker fee.
heroLead: Eighty Four is a name almost everyone in Pennsylvania recognizes from the lumber company headquartered here, but the mineral ground underneath the community is what matters to the families we work with.
intro: Eighty Four sits in a part of Washington County that's been core Marcellus wet-gas territory for well over a decade, with operators including Range Resources and EQT holding significant acreage across the surrounding townships. If your family owns farmland or an inherited interest near Eighty Four, there's a real chance nearby units have already produced meaningfully, which matters when we're evaluating what your interest is worth.
We buy Eighty Four-area mineral and royalty interests directly, and we check recent activity specific to your tract before ever discussing a number.

sections.heading: Core Wet-Gas Ground in Somerset and Nottingham Townships
paragraphs: The area around Eighty Four spans parts of Somerset and Nottingham townships, both of which have seen sustained Marcellus development for years. This is genuinely core acreage, not flank ground, which generally means more established production history and clearer nearby well data to evaluate against.
That said, whether your specific parcel has been leased or drilled still depends on the exact unit, so we check that directly rather than relying on the area's general reputation.

sections.heading: Farm Families With Long-Running Leases
paragraphs: A lot of the working farms around Eighty Four signed their first Marcellus lease during the initial leasing wave in the mid-to-late 2000s, and many have been under lease, and often producing, ever since. If your family's lease is one of those long-running ones, we review the actual terms and current statement as part of evaluating your interest, since older leases can carry different deduction language than what's become standard more recently.

sections.heading: What Act 13 Impact Fees Do and Don't Cover
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Act 13 impact fee gets paid by the operator directly to the county and local municipalities, funding things like road repair and emergency services, not your individual royalty check. A lot of Eighty Four-area owners assume impact fee revenue somehow offsets what's deducted from their own statement, and it doesn't. We're glad to explain that distinction plainly if your statement has you confused.

faqs.answer: Yes, this part of Washington County has been core wet-gas territory for years, though we still check the specific activity near your parcel.

faqs.question: My family's lease near Eighty Four is old, from the first leasing wave. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can. Early leases sometimes carry different deduction terms than what's become standard since. We review the actual lease as part of evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: Does the Act 13 impact fee affect my personal royalty check?
faqs.answer: No. Act 13 fees are paid by the operator directly to the county and local municipalities, separate from your individual royalty payment.
